description: The IC is marked 'ARM7'. However, the datasheet (page 1, 9) clearly states that the STM32F107xx series uses an 'ARM® 32-bit Cortex®-M3 CPU'. The ARM7TDMI is an older and different ARM core architecture. Marking a Cortex-M3 device as 'ARM7' is technically inaccurate and highly misleading, raising significant concerns about the authenticity or specifications of the installed die. This deviation from the specified core type is a strong indicator of potential misrepresentation.

The pin-1 indicator dot on the physical IC is located in the top-right corner of the package relative to the orientation of the printed text. In contrast, the datasheet's marking example for LQFP64 (Figure 48, page 90) consistently shows the pin-1 indicator dot in the top-left corner relative to the text orientation. This is a fundamental discrepancy in standard package marking conventions and factory practices, strongly suggesting a non-genuine part or a part manufactured outside ST's standard quality control.

The presence of two distinct date/lot code sequences ('G0243 93' and 'CHN G0 912') on separate lines deviates from the single 'Y WW' format shown in the datasheet's marking example (Figure 48). While not a definitive anomaly, it is an unusual variation in the marking layout that could indicate non-standard manufacturing or tracing practices.
